Items.Authors: Alex Drlica-Wagner, Alessio Taranto, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Joshua E. Meyers, John Andrew, Douglas R. Neill, Christian Aguilar, Brian Stalder, Robert H. Lupton, Aashay Pai, Lee S. Kelvin, Aaron E. Watkins, Luca Rosignoli, Hannah M. Pollek, Anastasia Alexov
Items.Title: Investigation and mitigation of a prominent off-axis stray light path in Rubin Observatory commissioning
Items.Abstract: The "scratched tape" stray light feature is the most prominent and prevalent stray light artifact identified during the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The scratched tape feature originates when light from large off-axis angles (~20 deg) passes between the mid-level and center-section light baffles, reflects off the primary mirror (M1), and illuminates the LSST Camera focal plane. This scenario represented an unobstructed stray light path to the sky during Rubin commissioning due to delays in the integration of the dome slit light-wind screen. This document describes the identification, modeling, characterization, and mitigation of the scratched tape stray light artifact.

Items.Authors: Ioannis Apergis, Dan Bayliss, Leonidas Asimakoulas, Paul Chote, James McCormac, Morgan Mitchell
Items.Title: Lab and on-sky testing of Andor Toran CMOS camera for astronomical applications
Items.Abstract: We present laboratory and on-sky performance results for the Toran, a new scientific CMOS camera from Oxford Instruments Andor, tested in its Low Noise (LN) and High Well Capacity (HWC) modes. Laboratory measurements show read noise of 1.07 e⁻ (LN) and 2.79 e⁻ (HWC), dark-signal non-uniformities of 0.076 e⁻ and 0.173 e⁻, and well depths of 15,700 e⁻ and 50,100 e⁻, corresponding to dynamic ranges of 83.39 and 85.05 dB. The detector exhibits excellent linearity (>99.8%) and low PRNU (<0.08%). Dark current is extremely low at 0.001 e⁻ pix⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 0 °C. On-sky tests at the TWenty Inch Survey Telescope (TWIST) at the Roque de Los Muchachos observatory in La Palma, Spain, show that HWC becomes camera-noise limited for faint stars due to its higher read noise, while LN consistently delivers superior photometric precision. These results highlight Toran as a strong candidate for high-precision time-domain astronomy.

Items.Authors: Marcelo Said Tala Pinto, Marshall Johnson, Julia Brady, Xavier Lesley, Jonathan Crass, Allie Renshaw, Michael Engelman, Brian Sands, Daniel Pappalardo, Christian Schwab, Julian Stürmer, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Matheus J. Castro, Stanimir Letchev, Thomas Legero, Ondrej Kitzler, Jacob Pember, Richard Pogge, Justin R. Crepp, Andrew Bechter, Eric Bechter
Items.Title: Laboratory characterization of iLocater
Items.Abstract: We present the latest laboratory characterization and optimization of the iLocater diffraction-limited, high-resolution near-infrared spectrograph. Our work focuses on measuring and optimizing optical performance, spectral resolution, and instrument stability. An iterative OpticStudio-guided focusing procedure improved optical alignment and spot quality across the detector. Using a Fabry–Pérot etalon and UNe lamps, we assessed resolving power and short- and long-term stability under controlled environmental conditions. We report updated optical and thermal performance metrics and instrument readiness for on-sky commissioning.

Items.Authors: Zhanshan Wang, Tian Lan, Jun Yu, Wenbin Li, Zeyi Ye, Yue Yu, Li Jiang, Chun Xie
Items.Title: Laboratory-based calibration system for the extreme ultraviolet spectrometer in 55 to 140nm wavelength range
Items.Abstract: IPOE has developed a laboratory-based calibration system for the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) imaging spectrometer in 55- to 140-nm. Utilizing a RF-produced gas-discharge light source, a grazing-incidence monochromator and an off-axis parabolic mirror to obtain a 50-mm-diameter collimated beam. The system characterizes key parameters of the spectrometer, including dark-field signal, wavelength, spectral resolution, spatial resolution, field of view, system efficiency, and effective area. The calibration process and results are presented and comparatively analyzed.

Items.Authors: Yang Gao, Wen Chen, Xuliang Duan, Kun Chen, Duojin Zheng, Yingquan Yang, Rong Shu, Junfei Li, Yonghe Chen, Jian Ge
Items.Title: Layered thermal design for ultraprecision photometry of the Earth 2.0 space mission
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) space mission required to detect Earth-sized exoplanets via the transit method demands exceptional thermal stability. The mission's thermal control system must counteract environmental heating flux and significant internal heat generated by equipment. In order to achieve this goal, a layered thermal design method has been applied, with a precisely thermal controlled optical bench made of low thermal expansion coefficient C-SiC material, a thermally control shield around the optical bench, flexible supporting truss isolating platform thermal flux, and a big multi-layer sun-shield resisting against the direct solar flux. This paper introduce the structural and thermal design of the spacecraft, focusing on the ultra-stable thermal design as well as simulation and test with a cut-off optical bench.

Items.Authors: Maggie Y. Kautz, Fernando E. Coronado, Austin Mears, Cameron C. Ard, Douglas M. Kelly, Luke D. Mayer, Sanchit Sabhlok, Jane E. Morrison, Andre F. Wong, Mike Eiklenborg, Heejoo Choi, Youngsik Kim, Steve Meyer, Patrick J. Ingraham, Nicholas J. Emerson, Mickael Rigault, Gudmundur K. Stefansson, Thomas Wevers, Daewook Kim, Catherine D. Merrill, Ewan S. Douglas
Items.Title: Lazuli Space Observatory’s widefield context camera
Items.Abstract: The Lazuli Space Observatory is a 3-meter aperture astronomical facility with a suite of instruments that will be utilized for rapid response observations. It is scheduled for launch in 2028. The Widefield Context Camera (WCC) is a 350–1100 nm multi-field imager spanning 35’ x 12’. This instrument provides both fine guidance and science capabilities. It is a mosaic of 23 commercial CMOS imagers with individual photometric filters. Two rows of Sony IMX 455 CMOS sensors will be used as science detectors, with two sensors defocused for wavefront sensing. One row of BAE HWK 4123 qCMOS sensors will be used for guiding and pointing. The HWK 4123 features a sub-electron readout noise (RON) that is pivotal for reaching >99% guide star availability in the field for closing of the observatory fast-steering mirror (FSM) control loop. There are two instrument apertures within the mosaic, passing light to the ExtraSolar Coronagraph (ESC) and the Integral Field Spectrograph (IFS).

Items.Authors: András Péter Joó, Bendegúz Koncz, Rebeka Gyöngyi Kiss, Örs Hunor Detre, Gyula Zilizi, Zsolt Bagoly, István Rácz, Sándor Pintér, István Horváth, Péter Koczák, János Szőke, Knud Jahnke, L. Viktor Tóth
Items.Title: LED-based calibration for the THESEUS InfraRed Telescope: calibration unit design concept
Items.Abstract: The InfraRed Telescope (IRT) on the THESEUS ESA M7 mission candidate requires precise radiometric calibration to enable accurate localisation and spectroscopy of high-energy transients. We present the conceptual design of the IRT’s LED-based Calibration Unit, developed to provide highly uniform and temporally stable illumination across five NIR bands, compliant with tight volume and critical alignment requirements. The design builds upon the heritage and demonstrated in-flight performance of the Euclid NISP Calibration Unit, offering valuable guidance for stability, packaging, and long-term behaviour of infrared LEDs in space. The concept targets sub-percent radiometric accuracy, supporting THESEUS’s infrared measurement goals and advancing future space-based NIR instrumentation. The resulting design is compact, lightweight, easy to manufacture and service, with robust performance in preliminary structural, thermal, and optical analyses.

Items.Authors: Arno P. Schoenmakers
Items.Title: Lessons learned: enhancing synchronization in the hardware and software development for the LOFAR upgrade
Items.Abstract: The Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR), one of the worlds largest radio telescopes, underwent significant modernization after its original construction between 2009 and 2012. This update required a comprehensive overhaul of its ageing signal processing technology and on-board software systems. A key challenge emerged due to the differing development approaches of the hardware teams, who worked in traditional iterative cycles spanning up to several months, and the software teams, who used Agile Scrum with rapid, three-weekly iterations. This caused planning misalignment and other issues during the project. To reconcile this we attempted to better synchronize the planning cycle. This improved collaboration and communication between the various disciplines involved in the development of the LOFAR update.

Items.Authors: Ashtyn Earl, Jamil Fayyad, Todd Charter, Maaike A. van Kooten, Kate Jackson, Jean-Pierre Véran, Homayoun Najjaran
Items.Title: Leveraging machine learning for PWFS reconstruction: bench validation with REVOLT
Items.Abstract: The pyramid wavefront sensor (PWFS) is well known for its sensitivity and is gaining popularity in adaptive optics (AO) systems, but its strong nonlinearity under large wavefront errors limits its dynamic range. Conventional AO systems address this with optical modulation, which linearizes the PWFS response at the cost of sensitivity and added complexity. Machine learning (ML) provides an alternative by reconstructing the PWFS output without modulation, preserving its intrinsic sensitivity. We present a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based reconstructor trained and validated using unmodulated PWFS data from the Research, Experiment, and Validation of adaptive Optics on a Legacy Telescope (REVOLT) platform at NRC Herzberg. Bench testing demonstrates accurate prediction of deformable mirror commands across diverse wavefront conditions, confirming the feasibility of ML-based reconstruction for PWFS. Future work will extend this approach to on-sky operation with REVOLT.

Items.Authors: Man-Yin Leo Lee, Shelley A. Wright, Renate Kupke, Aaron Brown, Jérôme Maire, Reagen Leimbach, Bryson Cale, James Wiley, Leo Y. Alcorn, Ted Aliado, Jerry Cabak, Maren Cosens, Chris Johnson, Tucker Jones, Marc Kassis, Andrew Kramer, Evan Kress, James Larkin, Nicholas MacDonald, Nathan Magari, Kenneth Magnone, Eric Wang, Kanaka Warad, Strawberry Wroolie
Items.Title: Liger at W.M. Keck Observatory: imager optical alignment
Items.Abstract: Liger is a near-infrared imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) for the Keck I telescope that will take advantage of the full capabilities of the upgraded Keck AO system. Liger covers a spectral range of 0.8 to 2.4 micron with a spectral resolution of R~4000-10000. It utilizes a sequential design that allows the imager and the spectrograph to operate simultaneously. The imager features a custom-designed camera that feeds the adaptive-optics-corrected image to one of two IFS channels: a slicer IFS or a lenslet IFS. The Liger imager assembly consists of two off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirrors, a flat fold mirror, a pupil wheel, a filter wheel, a pupil-viewing camera, and the Teledyne Hawaii-2RG detector. In this paper, we present the alignment procedure designed for the Liger imager assembly, along with a telescope simulator designed to mimic the light beam delivered by the Keck AO system to facilitate cryogenic performance verification of the imager.

Items.Authors: Ren-jie Zhao, Wen-qing Qu, Hao-ran Ma, Yu Ning, Feng Zeng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Low-Noise Readout electronics using high-speed digitalization scheme for MCT Detectors
Items.Abstract: This work focuses on developing a low-noise readout electronics using a high-speed digitalization scheme for Mercury Cadmium Telluride (MCT) infrared focal-plane detectors, which are widely used in astronomical observations due to their high sensitivity and excellent low-temperature performance. To meet the requirements of faint-object imaging, the system employs a 500 kHz pixel readout clock combined with a 20 MHz ADC oversampling architecture. High-speed oversampling allows the readout chain to capture multiple samples within each pixel period, enabling subsequent digital filtering and weighted averaging to effectively reduce temporal noise, suppress quantization and electronic interference, and improve the overall signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed method achieves low-noise readout without sacrificing frame rate, offering a practical solution for high-performance infrared astronomical imaging..

Items.Authors: Li Ji, Zheng Lou, Shu Niu, Wei Liu, Mingsheng Cai, Sen Wang, Yuan Qian, Shuping Yan, Shuinai Zhang, Keqiang Qiu, Shuangying Li, Jinlong Zhang, Peng Chen, Zhengxiang Shen, Zhanshan Wang, Chen Xu, Fu Li, Sebastian Diebold, Norbert Kappelmann, Beate Stelzer, Klaus Werner
Items.Title: Lyman UV exploration: present and far
Items.Abstract: Historically, progress in Lyman UV emission mapping has been constrained by the availability of advanced optical  coatings, high-performance gratings, and sensitive detectors. Over the past decade of development in China,  we have achieved significant breakthroughs across all these technological fronts. Specifically, we have developed  Al/LiF/eMgF2 mirror coatings that meet the reflectance requirements for the CAFE prototype across the 102–108  nm range. Concurrently, our concave VLS blazed gratings have demonstrated high diffraction efficiency near  the Ovi band with acceptable groove-density control. In addition to these optical advances, we discuss recent  progress in integral field spectroscopy within China, report on the vacuum-ultraviolet characterization of the  GSENSE2020BSI-PS scientific CMOS detector from 58 to 200 nm, and present the assembly and performance  evaluation of the prototype of CAFE scientific payload.

Items.Authors: Ole Streicher, Anastasia Galkin, Clare Worley
Items.Title: Machine-readable data models for robust data curation and release in 4MOST
Items.Abstract: Machine-readable data models are central to ensuring data integrity during 4MOST data curation and release. They provide formal, structured descriptions of complex raw and reduced data, enabling automated validation, consistent quality checks, and reproducible transformations. Within the 4MOST Pre-Release Access Point (4PRAP), these models support reliable coordination across heterogeneous workflows, from commissioning to archival. The poster presents the approach adopted to enforce data integrity using structured, machine-actionable models, illustrating their role in robust data management and preparation of science-ready 4MOST data products.

Items.Authors: Mauro Focardi, Sebastiano Ligori, Anna Maria Di Giorgio, Vito Capobianco, Donata Bonino, Natalia Auricchio, Leonardo Corcione, Vladimiro Noce, Pierpaolo Merola, Marina Vela Nuñez, Simone Chiarucci, Maria Farina, Marianna Michelagnoli, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta, Edoardo Rossi, Alessandra Tortora, Luca Serafini, Selene Salvetti, Alessio Pannocchia, Fulvio De Persio, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Tommasi Di Vignano, Navin K. Shivapa Kamble, Giovanni Giusi, Andrea Russi, Marius Stoica, Scige Liu, Emanuele Pace, Giampaolo Preti, Benoît Horeau, Michel Berthé, Christophe Cara, José Maria Gomez, Laura Martì, Andrew Caldwell, Paul Eccleston, Alexander Davidson, Rachel Drummond, Gianluca Morgante, Giuseppe Malaguti, Giuseppina Micela, Giovanna Tinetti, Caroline Simpson, Eduardo Medinaceli
Items.Title: Manufacturing and testing the avionic and engineering models of the instrument control unit of the ARIEL mission: an overview of the unit implementation and verification status following its critical design review
Items.Abstract: ARIEL is the M4 mission of the ESA’s Cosmic Vision 2015-2025 program, whose aim is to chemically characterise by low-resolution transit spectroscopy the atmospheres of over one thousand exoplanets orbiting nearby stars.  ARIEL hosts two scientific instruments, AIRS (ARIEL IR Spectrometer) and FGS (Fine Guidance Sensor) performing spectroscopy and spectro-photometry in the VIS and NIR range. AIRS is managed by an Instrument Control Unit (ICU), a Spacewire/PUS (Packet Utilization Standard) remote terminal, whose architecture and general status will be provided in this paper, including a summary of the main processing tasks implemented on-board its processor, following the closeout of the Critical Design Review (CDR) and the development and testing of the on-board Application SW (ASW) versions for both the Avionic (AVM) and Engineering (EM) models.

Items.Authors: Zhemin Cai, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Chris Coote, Timothy Chin, Jonathan Moller, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Helen McGregor, Jessica Zheng, Jonathon Lawrence, Yizheng Wang, Dani Guzman, Esra Kirkac, Cagatay Kirkac, Jake Linden, Michael Goodwin, Nick Cerneaz
Items.Title: Material selection and performance analysis of the GNAO adaptive optical bench system under gravity, thermal, and vibration loads
Items.Abstract: This paper presents a focused material selection and performance assessment for the Gemini North Adaptive Optics (GNAO) bench, a key element of the next-generation AO system for the 8-meter Gemini North telescope. Finite element analysis in Ansys Mechanical examined gravity-vector changes, thermal expansion, and vibration response, while Zemax optical modeling verified that resulting deformations remained within tolerance. Three materials were evaluated: fiber composite, stainless steel, and aluminum. The study found clear trade-offs in stiffness, thermal behavior, and cost. Although composites reduce mass and stainless steel offers high strength, an all-aluminum structure provides the best balance of performance, stability, and cost for the final design.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Simone Doniselli, Enrico Pinna, Marco Bonaglia
Items.Title: MAVIS: alignment tolerance analysis for the natural guide star wavefront sensor and acquisition camera
Items.Abstract: This work presents a Monte-Carlo alignment tolerance analysis of the Natural Guide Star Wavefront Sensor (NGS WFS) and Acquisition Camera (Acq Cam), key subsystems of the MAVIS instrument for the VLT. The study quantifies residual alignment errors after opto-mechanical integration, examining all relevant degrees of freedom of critical optical components. For the NGS WFS, 1500 MC replicas in 1×1 and 2×2 configurations show that residual Wavefront Error and spot radius stay within requirements. For the Acq Cam, a merit-function optimization minimizes on-axis RMS spot size and evaluates performance at maximum field. Results from 2000 MC replicas confirm compliance even in worst-case conditions. Overall, the analysis validates the robustness of the mechanical design and alignment procedures.

Items.Authors: Andrew W. Kruse, Israel J. Vaughn, Dionne Haynes, Trevor Mendel, Antony Galla, Brent Miszalski, Richard McDermid, Nuwanthika Fernando, Nuria Lorente, Miguel Gonzalez-Bolivar
Items.Title: MAVIS: calibration unit Fabry-Perot etalon design and simulation
Items.Abstract: The MAVIS Spectrograph provides two spatial resolutions and four spectral modes, with spectral resolutions of R ~ 4000-7000 over 370-695 nm or 495-935 nm, R ~ 11000-13000 over 630-880 nm, or R ~14000-15000 over 425-550 nm. The wavelength calibration of the spectrograph is enabled by a combination of natural emission lines and a full-spectrum of Fabry-Perot etalon peaks. The transmission spectrum of the etalon was simulated using a custom software package that incorporates the various effects on the finesse and location of the peaks, including the wavelength-dependent cavity length due to the phase of the dielectric coating. This effect is a crucial factor for evaluating the robustness of wavelength calibration algorithms. This is especially true for the MAVIS calibration, due to the large spectral bands where the phase of the coating varies significantly. Transmission peak thermal stability was modelled using the thermal expansion of the spacer and the dielectric coating layers.

Items.Authors: Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Antony Galla, Gaston Gausachs, Brian W. Taylor, Annino Vaccarella, Marco Bonaglia, Mirko Colapietro, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Enrico pinna, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Maria Bergomi, Valentina Viotto, François Rigaut, David Brodrick, Richard M. McDermid, Jennifer Burgess
Items.Title: MAVIS: FDR mechanical design of the adaptive optics module
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (MCAO Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics instrument for VLT's UT4, delivering corrected fields of view to a spectrograph, imager, and visiting instrument. Following Final Design Review, we present the Adaptive Optics Module (AOM) mechanical architecture. The optical bench supports post-focal relay optics (ADC, K-mirror derotator, deformable mirrors, selector) and rigidly mounts the calibration unit, guide star modules, and imager. The Overall Mechanical Structure connects to the Nasmyth platform while supporting the spectrograph and providing environmental isolation. We present final design solutions emphasizing the K-mirror system, material selection, and mechanical adhesive selections, with validation through thermoelastic, modal, and structural analyses.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Salvatore Savarese, Sergio D'Orsi, Pietro Schipani, Giulio Capasso, Gregory Jolley, Lewis G. Waller, Brian Taylor, Bernardo Salasnich, Elia Costa, David Brodrick, Gaston Gausachs, Stefan Ströbele, Pierre Haguenauer, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Tristan Monnier, Annino Vaccarella, Mark Downing, Dionne Haynes, Antony Galla, Maria Bergomi, Enrico Pinna, Fabio Rossi, Valentina Viotto, Jennifer Burgess, Francois Rigaut, Roger Haynes, Paolo Cerpelloni, Luca Marafatto, Kalyan Radhakrishnan Santhakumari
Items.Title: MAVIS: overview of the control electronics final design
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (the MCAO-Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a next-generation instrument for the ESO Very Large Telescope (VLT).  It includes Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics (MCAO) module with an advanced Imager and Spectrograph, supported by a dedicated calibration unit. All subsystems are housed within an enclosure to ensure thermal stability throughout the observing night.  The instrument control electronics are housed in eight actively cooled cabinets distributed across three different levels. The control electronics architecture adopts a modular approach that simplifies integration: three PLC CPUs are dedicated to controlling and monitoring all instrument functions, while a fourth CPU is fully dedicated to the Cryo-Vacuum System.  This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the final design of the MAVIS Control Electronics, detailing the architectural choices, subsystem interfaces, control cabinet layout and the implementation of the telemetry, interlock, and safety systems.

Items.Authors: Matteo Aliverti, Mirko Colapietro, Simone Doniselli, Salvatore Savarese, Luca Marafatto, Stefan Ströbele, Gaston Gausachs, Marco Bonaglia, Valentina Viotto, Maria Bergomi, David Brodrick, François Rigaut, Jennifer Burgess
Items.Title: MAVIS: PFR and NGS mechanical prototyping
Items.Abstract: MAVIS (MCAO Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph) is a Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics instrument for VLT's UT4, delivering corrected fields of view to multiple science channels. Following Final Design Review, we present key prototyping activities for the Post Focal Relay and Natural Guide Star module: deformable mirror alignment system, patrolling stage, and K-mirror assembly.  The DM alignment system employs dummy elements replicating mirror positions, with cable management testing for 8-meter deployment. The patrolling stage was characterized for motion accuracy.  K-mirror prototyping validated wobble, runout, and pupil shift requirements. Tests demonstrated exceptional repeatability, negligible backlash, and tracking performance exceeding specifications. Mirror alignment achieved sub-5-micrometer accuracy with 1-micrometer gravitational deformation. Tests validate design compliance and inform final optimization.

Items.Authors: Fabio D'Anca, Michela Todaro, Ugo Lo Cicero, Luisa Sciortino, Gabriele Minervini, Enrico Bozzo, Philippe Peille, Elise Bellouard, Sebasten Clamagirand, Gael Parot, Edoardo Cucchetti, Lander Ruiz de Ocenda, Thomas Gilet, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Mechanical design of the NewAthena X-IFU thermal filters supporting the technology readiness assessment
Items.Abstract: The NewAthena mission's X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) uses four thermal filters (THFs) to attenuate infrared and radio-frequency radiation from the spacecraft environment and to protect the cryogenic detector from particulate contamination, and to attenuate UV/Vis light from astrophysical sources. All these functions must be ensured while maintaining high X-ray transparency. During phases A and B, extensive studies have been conducted to optimize the mechanical design and to characterize the technology by environmental testing, demonstrating robustness for space applications. The investigations involved two membrane types: polyimide and carbon nanotube (CNT). This work presents the mechanical design of the THFs for the technology readiness assessment, along with preliminary results from FEM analysis and experimental testing. These developments represent a key step toward achieving the Technology Readiness Level 5 (TRL5) required for the subsequent phases of the Athena mission.

Items.Authors: Hannah Mary Margaret Pollek, Gabriele Rodeghiero, John Andrew, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Alessio Taranto, Luca Rosignoli, Aashay Pai, Douglas R. Neill, Travis Lange, Andrew P. Rasmussen, Aaron Roodman, Pierre Antilogus, Alexandre Boucaud, Martin Nordby
Items.Title: Mechanical studies of an additional light baffle for the LSST camera
Items.Abstract: During the commissioning of the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory, much concurrent work was performed to identify and mitigate the effects of stray light to minimize impacts that it may have on the Legacy Survey of Space and Time. The detailed Zemax models produced have found that the addition of a mechanical baffle inside of the LSST Camera has the potential to mitigate a notable portion of the identified stray light artifacts. This paper presents the mechanical studies regarding feasibility of installing one such a baffle near the third lens (L3), and the ideal geometry to maximize benefit to the survey. The primary topics considered are the space limitations and access needed to install it, material and coating possibilities, and potential thermal impacts of this added hardware.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Ferrari Barusso, Flavio Gatti, Edvige Celasco, Manuela Rigano, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Gabriele Minervini, Giacomo Gorla, Matteo D'Andrea, Claudio Macculi
Items.Title: Methods on the TRL-5 assessment for the production of the CryoAC chip for X-IFU NewAthena
Items.Abstract: The Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence detector (CryoAC) is a key subsystem of the newAthena X-IFU, designed to reduce cosmic-ray–induced background in the TES array. This work outlines the development of the fabrication processes and product-assurance activities required to meet ESA standards for space instrumentation. After validating the procedures, a batch of Demonstration Models (DM 1.2) was produced. The fabrication effort focuses on precise superconducting film transitions, reliable microfabrication, and strict environmental control. Complementary product-assurance activities include repeatability checks, vibration tests, and verification of procedural clarity. The results provide a roadmap for the future production and qualification of CryoAC units, emphasizing the importance of manufacturing accuracy and rigorous quality assurance coordinated by ASI.

Items.Authors: Felix C. M. Bettonvil, Chad Salo, Sander Kwast, Jeff Lynn
Items.Title: METIS risk management
Items.Abstract: The Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) is one of the four first-generation scientific instruments for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). METIS, designed to operate in the mid-infrared wavelength range, aims at both imaging, spectroscopy and coronagraphy. METIS is now in its manufacturing, assembly, integration and test phase (MAIT), and started recently the System AIT phase. The METIS project is of a substantially bigger scale than previous VLT projects, but still smaller than space missions. In this paper we present the risk management of METIS, both in terms of strategy, decision taking, costing and lessons learned.

Items.Authors: Henk J. van Weers, Johannes Dercksen, Geert Keizer, Brian Jackson, Roland den Hartog, Emanuele Taralli, Martin de Wit, Elinde Crama, Simon van Alphen, Indira Tjaden, Richard Groefsema, Alex Simon
Items.Title: Microvibration test-program of the X-IFU focal plane assembly development model 1.1
Items.Abstract: This work describes the micro-vibration measurement setup realized for the XIFU Focal Plane Assembly Development Model 1.1 (FPA DM1.1). It shows an approach based on measurement of the rigid body motion at the FPA interfaces. This with the purpose to overcome the high modal density of mechanical resonances present in the commercial cryogenic test bed in the frequency range of interest. These rigid body motions are also compared to the responses predicted by Finite Element Modelling (FEM). The micro-shaker units are developed in house and optimized for cryogenic use within the 40 Hz to 1 kHz range.

Items.Authors: María Concepción Cárdenas Vázquez, Daniel Ahrer, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Armin Huber, Ralf-Rainer Rohloff, Silvia Scheithauer
Items.Title: MITESI, mini ELT telescope simulator: from the concept to the real hardware in the lab
Items.Abstract: MITESI, MIni elt TElescope SImulator, is a project to produce a tool with specialized features and dedicated functionalities to test and verify ELT instrument requirements in the laboratory before on-telescope deployment.   Its first application is the performance verification of the METIS Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) subsystem at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy. It combines an opto-mechanical setup with advanced features for adaptive optics testing, including a deformable mirror, a diffraction-limited light source, and a real-time post-DM image monitoring system. It is capable of reproducing key ELT characteristics—such as atmospheric wavefronts, an ELT-shaped pupil, 1–4 µm broadband operation, a wide field of view, and an M5 simulator.  The system is currently in the validation. This contribution outlines its requirements, implemented functionalities, final optical and opto-mechanical designs, and associated tolerance analysis.

Items.Authors: Giacomo Cherchi, Fabrizio Cogato, Nicolas Gorius, Isabella Pagano, Gianalfredo Nicolini, Elisabetta Tommasi Di Vignano, Alessio Aboudan, Jose Lorenzo Alvarez, Matthias Ammler-von Eiff, Paolo Appollonio, Thierry Appourchaux, Claudio Arena, Natalia Auricchio, Ann Baeke, Nicolas Beraud, Elisa Borreguero, Francesco Borsa, Daniele Brienza, Juan Cabrera, Flavia Calderone, Simonetta Chinellato, Mathieu Condamin, Fernando Conde, Cydalise Dumesnil, Philipp Eigmueller, Jacopo Farinato, Lorenza Ferrari, Maria Fuermetz, Andrea Galbiati, Sena Gomashie, Nathalie Gorter, Duncan Goulty, Davide Greggio, Denis Griessbach, Sascha Grziwa, Pierre Guiot, Aline Hermans, Vèronique Hervier, Joseph Huesler, Rik Huygen, David Kappel, Tom Kennedy, Wouter Laauwen, Lionel Lourit, Sean Madden, Demetrio Magrin, Miguel Mas-Hesse, Alexandra Mazzoli, Francesca Molendini, Francisco Montoro, Matteo Munari, Carsten Paproth, Martin Pertenais, Raffaele Piazzolla, Roberto Ragazzoni, Gonzalo Ramos Zapata, Heike Rauer, Sara Regibo, Maria Teresa Rodrigo, Pierre Royer, Jesus Saiz, Mario Salatti, Amaia Santiago, Francesco Santoli, Maria Angeles Sierra, Alan Smith, Guilhem Terrasa, Giovanni Tropea, Angel Louis Valverde, Tim A. van Kempen, Bart Vandenbussche, Dave Walton, Pierre-Amaury Westphal, James Windsor
Items.Title: Mitigation of the line start effect in PLATO normal camera CCDs for accurate read-out noise characterization
Items.Abstract: PLATO is ESA's M3 mission to detect and characterise exoplanets around bright solar-type stars using high-precision space photometry. The payload includes 26 cameras: 24 Normal Cameras (N-CAMs) for photometry and 2 Fast Cameras for bright targets and guidance. Each N-CAM hosts four CCDs, each read out on two sides. During thermal-vacuum tests, bias and dark frames are acquired to characterise the read-out noise (RON) of each side. The CCD bias exhibits a Line Start Effect (LSE), a column-dependent offset at line start that leads to a systematic overestimation of pixel-to-pixel noise and can cause RON to exceed its requirement. For each side, an LSE profile is derived by averaging bias frames along rows and subtracted before recomputing RON maps. After presenting the general framework and the analysis concept, in this presentation, we show how the LSE mitigation reducing high-noise tails and restoring compliance with the N-CAM noise requirement.

Items.Authors: Oisín Creaner, Cáthal McAleer, Gerhard Ulbricht, Gary Donegan, Colm Bracken, Mario de Lucia, Tom Ray
Items.Title: MKID simulation through automated geometry generation
Items.Abstract: We present a software package to generate geometry models of Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) at scale. Through a graphical user interface (GUI), the user can set resonator parameters such as inductor and capacitor dimensions. They can also adjust the granularity of the simulation . The software will then iteratively generate geometry files matching those parameters. By inputting these files to established simulation software, it is possible to simulate large numbers of MKIDs under both idealised and non-ideal conditions. This software thus enables MKIDs development teams to rapidly iterate their designs in silico while including more realistic allowances for fabrication tolerance.

Araya Cortes, Roberto Tighe, Holger Drass, Pablo Zorzi, Massimo Brescia
Items.Title: Modeling of the diffuse background produced by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory M2 baffle scattered light
Items.Abstract: The secondary mirror (M2) cell baffle on the Simonyi Telescope restricts the light that reaches the LSSTCam focal plane thereby also shaping the inner edge of the telescope optical pupil. This work studies the contribution to the background of the residual light scattered by the M2 baffle when illuminated by highly off-axis light beams. The study is based matching ray tracing simulation, in-dome multi-wavelength test campaign using a Collimated Beam Projector (CBP) and on-sky images. Simulations and tests infer the intensity and spatial distribution of background scattered light within the different LSSTCam filters for different star asterism and spectral stellar classes.

Items.Authors: Riccardo Campana, Alfonso Pisapia, Lorenzo Amati, Edoardo Borciani, Paolo Calabretto, Claudio Labanti, Giulia Mattioli, Ezequiel J. Marchesini, Ajay Sharma, Smiriti Srivastava, Enrico Virgilli
Items.Title: Modeling proton-induced activation background in high-energy space instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Proton-induced activation is a major background source for high-energy missions in low-Earth orbit, where trapped protons generate radioactive isotopes that reduce instrument sensitivity. Direct Monte Carlo simulations are computationally expensive because isotope production is rare and many decay events must be modeled. We present a fast, modular framework that separates isotope production, decay evolution, and detector-response synthesis. Production yields are obtained from monochromatic proton Geant4 simulations, activities from Bateman-equation solutions, and backgrounds from simulated isotope emissions. This approach reduces computational cost by orders of magnitude while preserving the accuracy of full simulations. We apply the method to the XGIS instrument of the proposed ESA M7 mission THESEUS, demonstrating its usefulness for rapidly evaluating design and operational choices in future high-energy missions.

Items.Authors: Peter J. Young, Roque Ruiz-Carmona, Crisitan Urrutia
Items.Title: Modernising GHOST’s image display: from JSky to a pure JavaFX implementation
Items.Abstract: The GHOST GUI, a Java-based interface for astronomical observations, originally used JSky, a Swing-based image display library developed by ESO and adopted by Gemini for their Observing Tool. Integration via SwingNode limited performance, as JSky depends on the outdated Java Advanced Imaging (JAI) library and does not exploit modern GPU acceleration.  To resolve these limitations, a new image display component, JavaFXImageViewer, was developed entirely in JavaFX. Early prototypes demonstrated substantial performance improvements, leading to a full replacement of the legacy JSky component. Development productivity was enhanced through the use of AI-assisted programming tools, which supported code generation, refactoring, and design exploration.  The new library has recently been commissioned, achieving up to 75× faster rendering of 6k × 6k images on a MacBook M2 Pro and up to 20× faster on a 32-core Intel Xeon server (without GPU).

Items.Authors: Florian Quatresooz, Kyliann Robert, Yoshimi Rokugawa, Kenta Sakabe, Kenta Nakamura, Yuma Abe, Cyril Petit, Aurélie Montmerle-Bonnefois, Gaël Kermarrec, David Alaluf, Nicolas Védrenne
Items.Title: Monitoring atmospheric turbulence from stellar observations at optical ground stations
Items.Abstract: Many optical ground stations (OGS) deployed for free-space optical communications now include adaptive optics  (AO), offering the opportunity to retrieve optical turbulence profiles from AO telemetry. At ONERA’s FEELINGS OGS near Toulouse, we recently demonstrated real-time estimation of refractive index structure parameter (Cn2) and wind profiles during satellite links. However, limited by the availability of satellites, we explore whether our approach can utilize stellar sources in the infrared instead of satellite downlinks. This raises challenges in exposure time, noise handling, and estimation accuracy, which are investigated in this work using ONERA’s and NICT’s turbulence emulation benches.

Items.Authors: Mahshid Shiri, Christian Eredia, Vincenzo Cianniello, Enrico Cascone
Items.Title: MORFEO at ELT: development and experimental validation of a high-precision, MPC-based modular motion control architecture
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay for ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  This document details the development and experimental validation of a modular motion and instrument control architecture engineered specifically for MORFEO’s mechanical subsystems. The design effectively manages complex subsystems to ensure operational synergy and long-term reliability.   The architecture is built upon a modular, industry-standard foundation, strategically chosen to prioritize system scalability and interoperability. A core innovation in this framework is the implementation of a Model Predictive Control (MPC) generator, which significantly enhances positioning accuracy and control performance. By establishing this robust, standardized control framework, the system effectively minimizes integration risks and provides a dependable, high-precision

Items.Authors: Christian Eredia, Mahshid Shiri, Vincenzo Cianniello, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Benedetti, Marco Bonaglia, Simonetta Chinellato, Vincenzo De Caprio, Ivan Di Antonio, Andrea Di Dato, Benedetta Di Francesco, Fabio Di Nicola, Gianluca Di Rico, Jacopo Farinato, Italo Foppiani, Tommaso Lapucci, Luca Marafatto, Edoardo Redaelli, Marco Riva, Marco Xompero, Andrea Di Rocco, Ludovico Teodori, Paolo Ciliegi, Enrico Cascone
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: general overview of the instrument control hardware design towards the final design review
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  This paper shows the evolution of the Instrument Control Hardware design of MORFEO, as it approaches the Final Design Review milestone. The design is developed to harmonise compliance with ESO standards, based on industrial paradigms such as PLC and fieldbus protocol, and the specific needs of the system.  In particular, a description of the main aspects and challenges of the design is given, including choice of electronics cabinet standard and of their internal layout, overall distribution of the various types of network that are available at the ELT, characterisation of the mirrors tip-tilt motorised functions, routing strategy, with a focus on the major developments in the last two years of the project.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Marco Bonaglia, Giorgio Pariani, Tommaso lapucci, lorenzo busoni, Marco Riva, Paolo Ciliegi, Andrea di Rocco, Giuseppe De Luca
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: LOR mechanical design and analysis update
Items.Abstract: The LOR subsystem of MORFEO is approaching the Final Design Review (FDR). The mechanical design has now reached the final stage before procurement. In this presentation, the implemented mechanical solution, the simulations performed, and the methodology adopted to account for gravitational deformations and the vibration induced by the FREDA camera on the LOR board will be described.  The design of the LOR allows for an easy transition of the optical configuration from 1×1 to 2×2 on sky.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo De Caprio, Vincenzo Cianniello, Amirkeyvan Hajihashemi, Mina Sibalic, Christian Eredia, Mahshid Shiri, Enrico Cascone, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Matteo Aliverti, Giorgio Pariani, Marco Riva, Jacopo Farinato, Demetrio Magrin, Luca Marafatto, Alessandro Ballone, Simonetta Chinellato, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Matteo Munari, Ivan Di Antonio, Gianluca Di Rico, Gabriele Umbriaco, Ludovico Teodori, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: mechanical design and subsystem interfaces improvement of the main structure from PDR to FDR
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. MORFEO has officially passed the Preliminary Design Review in February 2023 and it is entering the final design phase. The general overview of the mechanical design and subsystem interfaces for the Main Structure described in this paper is an improved configuration of the one presented at Preliminary Design Review in the first half of 2021.

Items.Authors: Federico Battaini, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Demetrio Magrin, Matteo Munari, Giorgio Pariani, Jacopo Farinato, Elena Carolo, Alessandro Ballone, Daphne Diretto, Marco Riva, Luca Rosignoli, Sophie Antonia Penger, Bernardo Salasnich, Alessio Taranto, Simone Di Filippo, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Gabriele Umbriaco
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: MiniTAC, a support equipment to test the LGSO focal and pupil planes
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  MORFEO will include six laser guide stars wavefront sensors (LGS-WFS).  It is critical to test the optical quality of the beam delivered to the LGS WFS in terms of focal ratio, telecentricity, pupil distortion, and asterism delivery position. To this end, we present MiniTAC, a support equipment integrating three channels: a focal plane PSF imager, a pupil imaging system and a SH-WFS, mounted on motorized stages for field-of-view and axial scanning.

Items.Authors: Matteo D'Ambrogio, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Nicholas Devaney, Niamh Fitzgerald, Daphne Diretto, Bernardo Salasnich, Marco Riva, Matteo De Magistris, Gabriele Umbriaco, Sophie Penger, Luca Rosignoli, Alessio Taranto, Luca Marafatto, Elena Carolo, Simone Di Filippo, Federico Battaini, Jacopo Farinato, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Marco Bonaglia, Lorenzo Busoni, Jean-Pierre Véran
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: optomechanical design of test alignment camera
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. The TAC (Test Alignment Camera) is a piece of equipment that will be installed inside the MES (MICADO Emulating Structure), under the LOR ( Low Order and Reference): its main function is to simulate and verify all the requirements regarding the interface between MORFEO and MICADO in the Bologna Integration Hall, before the whole system is sent to the ELT in Chile. The TAC is subdivided into Stage system, equipped with three linear stages – one for each axis – to precisely control the position of the assembly in space, and the Camera system, an aluminium plate housing sensors and the necessary optomechanics. This paper focuses on the optomechanical design of the TAC, presenting the overcome challenges and choices of equipment.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Rodeghiero, Benedetta Di Franceso, Ivan Di Antonio, Angelo Valentini, Gianluca Di Rico, Luca Rosignoli, Sylvain Oberti, Mauro Dolci, Simone Benedetti, Amico Di Cianno, Nicholas Devaney, Alexander Goncharov, Gabriele Umbriaco, Matteo Munari, Demetrio Magrin, Giorgio Pariani, Jacopo Farinato, Luca Marafatto, Alessandro Ballone, Lorenzo Busoni, Enrico Giro, Ludovico Teodori, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: paraxial calibration unit prototype alignment demonstration in the lab
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. The MORFEO calibration unit provides simultaneous natural and laser guide calibration sources to the multiple MORFEO wavefront sensors and the MICADO scientific field of view. The system adopts an optical design with many semi-reflective elements that leads to the presence of optical ghosts and an intrinsic low throughput. This work reports an empirical demonstration of the alignment strategy developed and tested exploiting a lab paraxial prototype.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Umbriaco, Diego Gilioli, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Alessio Taranto, Luca Rosignoli, Sophie Antonia Penger, Matteo Munari, Giorgio Pariani, Demetrio Magrin, Jacopo Farinato, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Luca Marafatto, Elena Carolo, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Simone Di Filippo, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: precision alignment of MORFEO’s laser guide star objective using MAT and PIP
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   A Micro Alignment Telescope (MAT) equipped with a Point-Image-Point (PIP) system was used to validate a ghost-based optical alignment method for the MORFEO Laser Guide Star Objective (LGSO). Ghost reflections from optical surfaces were used as intrinsic references to define the optical axis without the need for external targets. Laboratory tests on a prototype, analyzed through MAT imaging and Python centroid routines, achieved residuals of 5 µm in decenter and 10 asec in tilt. Simulations applied to the LGSO–MORFEO model predict alignment errors of ~10 µm and 2 asec, one order of magnitude below system tolerances (1 mm, 360 asec). The MAT+PIP technique thus proves to be a compact, self-referenced, and highly precise tool for MORFEO alignment and integration.

Items.Authors: Ludovico Teodori, Paolo Ciliegi, Andrea Di Rocco, Marco Riva, Demetrio Magrin, Lorenzo Busoni, Simonetta Chinellato, Jacopo Farinato, Italo Foppiani, Gianluca Di Rico, Vincenzo De Caprio, Gabriele Umbriaco, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Matteo Munari
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: procurement governance and gating strategy during the final design phase
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope, providing MCAO correction for MICADO and HARMONI. In MORFEO, procurement is a key element of Phase C (Final Design Phase) , where acquisition processes evolve with design maturity. Tender packages are released progressively, according to subsystem readiness and consolidated requirements and interfaces. Intermediate reviews, conducted with ESO, validate the completeness of each tender package and authorize early procurement of long-lead items, once parameters reach sufficient maturity. Early procurement mitigates schedule exposure but does not authorize fabrication, which will begin only after the Final Design Review. The contribution focuses on MORFEO’s procurement approach, outlining how early acquisition in Phase C and integrated design-to-manufacturing tenders contribute to system coherence and risk reduction.

Items.Authors: Jacopo Farinato, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Luca Marafatto, Gabriele Umbriaco, Marco Riva, Edoardo Redaelli, Demetrio Magrin, Vincenzo De Caprio, Vincenzo Cianniello, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Munari, Matteo D'Ambrogio, Hossein Mahmoodzadeh, Matteo Aliverti, Sylvain Oberti, Lorenzo Busoni, Nicholas Devaney, Jean-Pierre Véran, Marco Bonaglia, Thibaut Moulin, Italo Foppiani, Simonetta Chinellato, Luca Rosignoli, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Elena Carolo, Diego Gilioli, Giuseppe Di Luca, Simone Di Filippo, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Leonardo Buoncompagni, Alessio Taranto, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Andrea Baruffolo, Maria Bergomi, Giulio Capasso, Enrico Cascone, Manal Chebbo, Paolo Ciliegi, Mirko Colapietro, Elia Costa, Domenico D'Auria, Ivan Di Antonio, Benedetta Di Francesco, Chiara Di Prospero, Dafne Diretto, Gianluca Di Rico, Andrea Di Rocco, Mauro Dolci, Simone Doniselli, Christian Eredia, Enrico Giro, Alexander Goncharov, Laurent Jocou, Salvatore Lampitelli, Fulvio Laudisio, Alfio Puglisi, Edgard Renault, Bernardo Salasnich, Salvatore Savarese, Marcello Scalera, Mahshid Shiri, Rosanna Sordo, Ludovico Teodori, Angelo Valentini, Marco Xompero
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: the MAIT process in Europe, an update of the plan toward the instrument FDR
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For Elt Observations) is the post-focal AO module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The main purpose of MORFEO is to relay the light beam from the ELT focal plane to the client instruments (MICADO and HARMONI) compensating, through a MCAO system, the atmospheric turbulence and other disturbances affecting the wavefronts of the scientific targets.  The optical design of the instrument has been conceived in a way that there are very relaxed alignment tolerances for all the optical components but a single compensator, the second spherical Deformable Mirror, which is actuated in tip-tilt and piston (through a hexapod system) to fine tune the optical quality provided to the client instruments. Additionally, two flat folding mirrors, motorized in Tip-Tilt and Piston, are used to properly position the pupil and focal plane on the client instruments.  In this paper we describe the AIT process that will be performed at INAF-OAS Bologna.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Bernardo Salasnich, Daphne Diretto
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: thermal control system manifold prototyping
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   High thermal stability is critical for performance, necessitating a robust Thermal Control System (ThCS). This paper presents prototyping activities validating the ThCS architecture's ability to maintain temperature stability across MORFEO subsystems. We describe the thermal prototype design, including cooling strategies and control hardware selection. Performance tests characterized thermal response, controller performance, and system robustness under expected ELT operational conditions. Preliminary results confirm the prototype meets stability requirements, identifies critical interfaces, and guides design refinements. These activities significantly de-risk the final ThCS implementation, ensuring MORFEO's reliable telescope performance.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Ballone, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Demetrio Magrin, Jacopo Farinato, Leonardo Buoncompagni, Gabriele Umbriaco, Luca Rosignoli, Alessio Taranto, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Lorenzo Busoni, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Munari, Elena Carolo, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Matteo D'Ambrogio, Nicholas Devaney, Daphne Diretto, Fulvio Laudisio, Elia Costa, Bernardo Salasnich, Vincenzo Cianniello, Vincenzo De Caprio, Marco Riva, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Ludovico Teodori, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: updates on the optical fine alignment strategy
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. Multiple MORFEO fine Optical Alignment strategies are currently under investigation. For this contribution, we report updates on the “Donut” method. In this approach, residual low order aberrations - due to misalignments - are estimated by calculating the moments of light in out-of-focus images on the instrumental focal plane detector. MORFEO’s M10, M11 and M12 can then be moved to compensate for those and align the pupil and focal planes between MORFEO and the attached instruments. We present several tests to assess the performances of this strategy, also accounting for stray light effects and demonstrating using more realistic “on-sky” donuts. This study is performed by means of sequential and non-sequential simulations with the Zemax software and its API.

Items.Authors: Giuseppe De Luca, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Tommaso Lapucci, Marco Bonaglia
Items.Title: MORFEO@ELT: LOR Anti-Collision System Design and Test Validation
Items.Abstract: The Low Order and Reference (LOR) of MORFEO, the multi‑conjugate adaptive optics relay for the ELT, incorporates three axisymmetric optical benches equipped with pick‑off mirrors to track guide stars. The system geometry introduces potential collisions between arms and adjacent structures, requiring protective measures. An anti‑collision and damping system was developed, combining conductive contact detection with mechanical energy absorption to ensure safe operation. Validation through a dedicated mock‑up and experimental campaign confirmed the effectiveness of the approach. The architecture of the damping system, the mock-up design, and the results of the validation tests are presented here to provide a reference case for the design of next-generation instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Meghna Mohamed, Alessandro Meoli, Walter Seifert, Andreas Kelz, Myriam Rodrigues, Alondra Solá, Wenli Xu, Carlos Rodriguez Alvarez, Gavin Dalton, Thomas Augusteijn, Kacem El Hadi, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Rubén Sanchez-Janssen, Hermine Schnetler, Jay Stephan, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC on ELT: VIS channel transmission budget and estimates from SAR to preliminary design phase
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC for the 39 m ELT comes with MOS and mIFU capabilities in the wavelength range from 390 nm to 1800 nm and is currently in phase B2 leading up to PDR. The VIS Science Channel is intended to have separate low- and high-resolution fibre link feeds and a dual-beam two-camera design to split the spectrum (in blue and red arms), providing simultaneous coverage from 390 nm to 950 nm in low resolution and multiple high resolution bands in the same wavelength range. Transmission estimates of the VIS channel have helped in assessing potential risks in compliance and identifying the critical contributors impacting the transmission budget. This paper looks into VIS Channel transmission budget, the critical contributors impacting the transmission performance, and the evolution of the transmission estimates (and the methodology), from the System Architecture Review to the ongoing Preliminary Design phase.

Items.Authors: Dani Guzman, Nirmala Kunwar, Jake Linden, Slavko Mali, Cam Brown, Michael Boers, Jafar Shojaii, Mark Casali, Tayyaba Zafar, Benjamin Pope, Lee Spitler
Items.Title: MQ-Zero: ultracompact detector controller for in-vacuum FPA readout
Items.Abstract: The Readout Sensors Initiative (RSI) at Australian Astronomical Optics, Macquarie University develops detector readout electronics for astronomy, space missions, and related fields. This paper presents MQ-Zero, a prototype controller designed to demonstrate the feasibility of co-locating readout electronics with infrared focal plane arrays in vacuum cryogenic environments. MQ-Zero incorporates a modern signal chain, including a high-performance analogue-to-digital converter and an on-board field-programmable gate array, while addressing the thermal and mechanical constraints of in-vacuum operation. The compact form factor enables placement immediately adjacent to a detector, reducing cable capacitance and susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. A key focus of the current development phase is the thermal management strategy. This paper reports the design methodology, thermal modelling results, and preliminary electronics testing.

Items.Authors: Chiara D'Amato, Andrea Bianco, Giorgio Pariani, Fabrizio Fornasiero, Robert J. Harris, Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Sebastiaan Haffert, Aurelien Benoit, Viktoria Kutnohorsky, David MacLachlan, Tim Birks, Joss Guy, Robert R. Thomson, Jared R. Males, Laird M. Close, Olivier Guyon
Items.Title: Multicore integral field unit (MCIFU v2): design and optimization of the integral field spectrograph with multiplexed VPH gratings
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Core Integral Field Unit (MCIFUv2) is a unit enabling infrared integral field spectroscopy for the MagAO-X adaptive optics system on the Magellan Clay telescope. Its fibre-fed integral field spectrograph was designed and optimized for exoplanet atmosphere characterization in the near-infrared. The design achieves diffraction-limited performance across the Y, J, and H bands with medium spectral resolution (R = 5000-7880), using a novel configuration of multiplexed volume phase holographic gratings and custom optics. The system was optimised with theoretical modelling in MATLAB and ray-tracing in Zemax OpticStudio, obtaining an improved set of lenses to control aberrations across the wide operating bandwidth. The final design achieves high diffraction efficiency (> 80%), low crosstalk (< 1%), and a compact configuration, making it a suitable candidate for future integration with the MagAO-X extreme adaptive optics system.

Items.Authors: Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Robert J. Harris, Robbie Mears, Tim Birks, Aurélien Benoît, David MacLachlan, Chiara D'Amato, Sebastiaan Haffert, Andrea Bianco, Joss Guy, Viktoria Kutnohorsky, Robert R. Thomson, Jared R. Males, Olivier Guyon, Laird M. Close
Items.Title: Multicore integral field unit (MCIFU v2): fibre-link design and status
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Core Integral Field Unit (MCIFU v2) is an add-on for the MagAO-X adaptive optics system, enabling spectroscopy and spectral differential imaging of close companions such as protoplanets and exoplanets in the Y, J, and H bands at R~5000. MagAO-X provides a diffraction-limited focal plane, which the MCIFU samples using a 119-spaxel fibre link that relays a 1-arcsecond field-of-view to an external spectrograph. Two optimized fibre links are considered, one for Y+J (0.96–1.345 μm) and one for H (1.49–1.78 μm), each consisting of a Micro-Lens Array (MLA), a Multi-Core Fibre (MCF), and a photonic reformatter. A 3D-printed MLA enhances coupling into the MCF, whose Y+J design uses three dissimilar single-mode core types arranged to reduce crosstalk. At the output, an Ultrafast-Laser-Inscribed reformatter converts the hexagonal core layout into a linear slit with ~66% transmission and <5×10⁻⁴ crosstalk (simulation). The spectrograph then disperses all spaxels onto a HAWAII-2 detector.

Items.Authors: Philippe Voyer, Maya Amit, Steven J. Benton, Benjamin E. Boyd, Anthony M. Brown, Giulia Cerini, Paul Clark, Matthew Craigie, Christopher J. Damaren, Tim Eifler, Spencer W. Everett, Aurélien A. Fraisse, Leo WH Fung, Ajay S. Gill, Suren Gourapura, Eric Habjan, John W. Hartley, David Harvey, Bradley Holder, Eric M. Huff, Mathilde Jauzac, William C. Jones, David Lagattuta, Gavin Leroy, Jason SY Leung, Lun Li, Thuy Vy T. Luu, Richard Massey, Jacqueline E. McCleary, Adyn Miles, Johanna M. Nagy, C. Barth Netterfield, Emaad Paracha, Susan F. Redmond, Jason D. Rhodes, Andrew Robertson, L. Javier Romualdez, Sayan Saha, Jurgen Schmoll, Mohamed M. Shaaban, Ellen L. Sirks, Sut Ieng Tam, Simon Tartakovsky, Georgios N. Vassilakis, André Z. Vitorelli, Bryce J. Warren, Alfredo Zenteno
Items.Title: Multi-sensor fusion for fine-guidance and milli-arcsecond-level attitude estimation of balloon-borne telescopes
Items.Abstract: Balloon-borne telescopes rely on fine-guidance systems to achieve sub-arcsecond image stability despite residual disturbances from the balloon platform. In fine-guidance systems using a Fast Steering Mirror (FSM) driven by a single guide star, boresight roll can be be misinterpreted as image motion, leaving residual motion across the focal plane. This effect, referred to as roll leakage, becomes increasingly important for wide-field observatories. Using data from the 2023 SuperBIT science flight, roll leakage is characterized and a simulation framework combining optical ray tracing, asynchronous guide-star measurements, estimation, and FSM control is developed to evaluate mitigation strategies. Under realistic flight disturbances, multi-star estimation reduces average roll-induced science-field image motion by 31.8% for the SuperBIT geometry and 63.9% for a representative GigaBIT geometry. These results motivate multi-star fine guidance for future wide-field balloon-borne telescopes.
